extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers / Royal Society members (scientists conducting physical and chemical experiments)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and reporting original experimental observations about the superficial figures and interfacial behaviour of fluids, including apparatus, materials, and repeatable trials. Emphasises careful control of variables, purity of reagents, and detailed recording of phenomena without premature causal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and systematically vary the contiguous fluid
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether the surface figure of a liquid (e.g., concave meniscus) is altered by substituting the contiguous fluid (air, another liquor, spirit of wine, oil, deliquated salt of tartar, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: replace the air with spirit of wine, oil of turpentine, or common water in slender tubes and observe changes (concave → flat or convex). Varying the contiguous fluid is used as a primary controlled-variable test to probe surface behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use purified/dephlegmed reagents to avoid unintended mixing
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ highly rectified or dephlegmed spirit and other purified liquids so that 'phlegm' or impurities do not cause unintended union of phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text stresses using 'exquisitely dephlegmed' spirit of wine so oils will not mix; purity is necessary to maintain distinct surfaces and to interpret interfacial phenomena reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe fluids free from solid contact where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the aim is to study fluid–fluid interfaces, arrange experiments so portions of fluid are encompassed only by other fluids, not adhered to solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author uses drops suspended above an underlying liquor (in phials and slender pipes) so the surface is 'common to the two contiguous liquors' and not influenced by glass contact; contrast is drawn when the fluid is allowed to touch the inside of the glass, producing different figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat trials for greater security and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat experiments multiple times to confirm observed phenomena and to detect variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author repeatedly notes repeating trials (e.g., 'for greater security several times repeated') and reports when outcomes are not constant, indicating the need for replication to assess consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematically vary experimental parameters (quantity, height, agitation, density)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change one parameter at a time — amount/bulk of the added fluid, height/column of incumbent fluid, degree of agitation, relative densities — to observe how the surface figure depends on those factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete variations performed: altering the height of water incumbent on mercury, varying the bulk of oil (small drops → spheres; larger → hemispheres/ellipses), and changing agitation (moderate agitation deforms shapes; strong agitation breaks them into globes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for atmospheric pressure (use pneumatical receiver/vacuum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the influence of air by evacuating the surrounding atmosphere (pumping out the common air) and noting changes in surface figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author conveys slender tubes into a pneumatical receiver and exhausts air to compare behaviour under diminished air-pressure (e.g., some ambiguous effects on mercury; no sensible change for water), and cautions about bubbles confounding interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and account for artifacts and confounders (bubbles, foetid oil, phlegm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch for small bubbles, residual foetid oils, or other unseen subtile matters that may affect surface appearance and measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: bubbles observed in mercury under vacuum might influence observed protuberance; the author warns these may be 'suspected to have some interest in the phenomenon.' Ensure apparatus is as free from such artifacts as possible and report them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record optical and reflective properties of interfacial surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Document how interfaces reflect incident light and appear optically (e.g., bright/metallic reflection resembling quicksilver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes vivid reflections from conceivably flat physical surfaces between two liquids, sometimes 'almost like that of quicksilver', and records how tinged alcali with certain oils produced strong specular reflections. Optical appearance is a relevant observable to report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note scale-dependent shape changes (size/weight effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record how the size or bulk of droplets or aggregates affects their shape — small drops tend to be spherical, larger aggregates flatten or become hemispherical/elliptical under weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated observations: (1) small oily drops appear exactly spherical; (2) larger aggregates depress and appear elliptical; (3) yet larger portions form imperfect hemispheres or segments of a sphere depending on bulk and weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle agitation carefully; moderate agitation vs strong agitation effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use controlled, moderate agitation to observe reversible shape deformations; avoid strong agitation which produces breakup and irreversible formation of small globules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The account distinguishes effects of moderate agitation (various figurations that quickly recover) from too strong agitation (portions broken off and turned into little globes), advising conservative manipulation to preserve phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document irreversible behaviours and mixing hysteresis
rubrics_metrics.description: Report irreversible outcomes (e.g., once oils have united they are not easily parted) and note any hysteresis or permanent change caused by an operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author attempted to recombine oils to include another liquor between them but found that once oils united they would not be easily parted; such irreversible behaviours are important to record as they bear on reproducibility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate careful description of phenomena from causal inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer to fully describe observed phenomena first, without immediately asserting causes or consequences; leave causal analysis for later or separate discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author explicitly states an intention to 'take notice of the chief phaenomena ... without staying to inquire into the causes or the consequences of them,' highlighting a methodological principle of descriptive priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear description of materials, apparatus, and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the experimental set-up (e.g., slender glass tubes sealed at one end, bore diameter, phials half filled, positions relative to light and eye) and the nature of the materials used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the report the author gives apparatus details (tube bore 'not quite a quarter of an inch', sealed ends, phials half full, positioning for light), which are necessary to allow others to reproduce and interpret the observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify publication claims and quality of illustrative material
rubrics_metrics.description: In editorial/book-review contexts, check asserted endorsements or commissions and evaluate the quality of plates/illustrations and cataloguing claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from book review: a printed claim that six commissioners examined a treatise was false (one commissioner declared he never saw the treatise), and the plates for a diaphragm treatise were judged 'very indifferent' — indicating standards for verification and quality of illustrative content.
